messages.content: Small Texas wrinkle, sorry. The Wednesday coffee moved from Round Rock to Georgetown, and Delta just moved my AUS-SLC return about 35 minutes earlier. I still have the San Marcos room Monday and the north San Antonio room Tuesday. Do I keep Tuesday night in San Antonio or switch while I can?

I would lean toward switching if the new return is around 2:30 and the Tuesday dinner ends early enough to drive north afterward. Georgetown removes the riskiest piece: a very early San Antonio checkout, then coffee, then the airport on a tighter return. What is the new departure time, and when should the Stone Oak dinner wrap?
Return is 2:35 now. Dinner is in Stone Oak and should wrap at 8:00, maybe 8:15. I’ll have only a carry-on.

Then switch the final night. Tuesday: dinner ends 8:00-8:15, drive Stone Oak to Georgetown about 1:45-2:00, check in around 10:00-10:20. Wednesday: breakfast 6:30 or 7:00, checkout by 8:10, be at the 9:00 coffee calmly, leave Georgetown about 10:30, fuel near AUS, and return the rental around 11:50-noon. I would treat 12:20 as the latest comfortable rental return for a 2:35 flight.
Is breakfast realistic if I’m checking in that late?

Yes, as long as the hotel confirms late arrival and breakfast starts by 6:30 or 7:00. Pick a simple Georgetown or north Round Rock option near I-35 with free parking, included breakfast, and a 24-hour desk. Avoid anything that requires valet or a downtown-style garage that could slow you down Wednesday morning.
Okay, make the call. I can cancel San Antonio until 6 p.m. tomorrow.

Call: cancel the San Antonio room and book Georgetown tonight, refundable if possible. Check these items before you click: late check-in noted, breakfast start time, free parking, checkout at 11 or later even though you will leave earlier, and the cancellation deadline. If the Georgetown options are poor, use north Round Rock as the backup, not south Austin.
What do I do with luggage and fuel on Wednesday? I don’t want to be juggling the bag at the coffee.

Checkout before the coffee and leave the main carry-on locked in the trunk; take only a small tote or laptop bag inside. Park where the car is visible if the school lot allows it. After the coffee, leave by 10:30 if possible, 10:45 latest. Take the direct airport route, top off gas at an airport-area station, return the rental by noon, and keep the hotel cancellation, fuel, toll, parking, and rental receipts together.

messages.content: Texas is behind me. I need to start the Twin Cities yield trip for mid-April: Monday evening admitted-student reception in St. Paul, Tuesday 11:00 transfer fair in Bloomington, and Wednesday morning counselor breakfast in Minneapolis. Can you help me decide Sunday vs Monday arrival, car vs rideshares, and hotel zone before I place holds?
Yes. Two details will change the recommendation: where in St. Paul is the reception, and are you carrying materials yourself or shipping them ahead?

Reception is near Cathedral Hill, fair is by the Bloomington hotel/convention area, and the breakfast is near the North Loop in Minneapolis. I’m shipping two small boxes to the Monday venue and traveling with a carry-on. Budget target is under about $180 a night if possible.

For arrival, Sunday afternoon is the safer hold. A Monday morning nonstop can work on paper, but if the flight slides, baggage takes time, or ground transport is slow, you lose the recovery window before the reception. I would only use Monday morning if the savings are meaningful and you are comfortable going straight into event mode. A Monday afternoon arrival is too tight.
I can justify Sunday if the hotel cost doesn’t get silly. What zones would you compare?

Shortlist by zone: St. Paul near Cathedral Hill: easiest Monday night, good nearby dinner choices, but breakfast may be paid or unclear and parking often adds cost. Bloomington/MOA-I-494 area: usually stronger breakfast and free parking, easiest Tuesday, simple airport access, but you drive to St. Paul Monday. Minneapolis/North Loop: best for Wednesday and meals, but rates and parking are likely higher and it adds more Tuesday driving.
My instinct is Bloomington because of breakfast and parking. Is the Monday night drive to St. Paul annoying enough to avoid it?

Not enough to make me reject Bloomington. If the reception is at 6:00, leave Bloomington around 4:45 to allow traffic and parking. After the event, the return drive should be easier, likely 25-35 minutes. Tuesday becomes very easy, and Wednesday to North Loop is manageable if you leave early. St. Paul would save Monday hassle but costs you breakfast certainty and parking simplicity.
What about skipping the rental and using rideshares?

Rideshares are feasible from a St. Paul base, but they are less clean from Bloomington because you would need airport transfers plus Monday St. Paul, Tuesday fair, and Wednesday breakfast. Estimate roughly $160-$220 total depending on surge. A compact or midsize rental may be similar once you add fuel, but Bloomington hotels often offset that with free parking. Since you have three suburban/urban stops, I’d take the car if you choose Bloomington.
If I arrive Sunday, do I need the car immediately or could I rideshare to the hotel and pick one up Monday?

If you stay Bloomington, pick up the car at MSP Sunday. It saves a second airport trip and gives you flexibility for dinner, supplies, and Monday timing. If you stay St. Paul, a Sunday rideshare plus a Monday or Tuesday car pickup could work, but it adds logistics and does not help much once Tuesday and Wednesday are in different places.
Give me the tentative package and the reimbursement catches before I start holds.

Tentative package: arrive Sunday afternoon on a nonstop into MSP; return Wednesday after the counselor breakfast, ideally early to midafternoon; rent a car at MSP Sunday evening through Wednesday late morning; hold a cancellable Bloomington hotel with included breakfast and free parking; hold one St. Paul backup only if its cancellation is easy. Reimbursement checks: confirm Sunday night is covered, keep rental plus fuel and parking receipts, note any hotel parking charges, and verify whether breakfast is included or needs to be expensed. Also check each hotel cancellation deadline before placing holds.

messages.content: Twin Cities update. The Wednesday counselor breakfast moved from Minneapolis to a suburban school in Plymouth. Also the St. Paul reception released a room code around $169, but it doesn’t include breakfast. Bloomington is about $159 with breakfast and free parking. The Monday morning flight is still cheaper by about $85. Which way would you hold?
I’d like the exact Wednesday timing before I call it, because Plymouth changes the airport-return math. What time does the breakfast start and when can you realistically leave?
Breakfast is 8:00. I should be able to leave by 9:45, maybe 10:00 if conversations run long. Monday reception is 6:00-8:00, and Tuesday fair is 11:00-2:00.

With Plymouth in the mix, I would hold Sunday afternoon arrival, a rental car, and the Bloomington hotel. The $85 Monday-flight savings is not enough to give up the recovery buffer before the Monday reception. The St. Paul code is tempting for Monday night, but once you add paid breakfast and likely parking, Bloomington is still the cleaner three-night base.
Can you show the trade-off plainly?

Plain version: St. Paul code: best Monday evening, walkable dinner after the reception, but no breakfast, likely paid parking, Tuesday drive to Bloomington, and Wednesday drive to Plymouth. Bloomington: best Tuesday, breakfast included, free parking, easy airport access, Monday drive to St. Paul, and Wednesday drive to Plymouth. Minneapolis drops to third now because Plymouth replaced North Loop and Monday rates are inflated.
Would one night in St. Paul and then moving to Bloomington be smarter?

Only if you expect the reception to run late or you need to stay for dinner with hosts afterward. Otherwise, changing hotels adds checkout, luggage, and another check-in for a small gain. One Bloomington base is less fussy: arrive Sunday, unpack once, drive to St. Paul Monday, stay close to Tuesday’s fair, then drive to Plymouth Wednesday.
What rental timing should I use?

Pick up at MSP after the Sunday afternoon arrival and keep it through Wednesday late morning. For Wednesday, leave Plymouth by 9:45-10:00, allow 35-45 minutes to MSP, add 10 minutes to fuel, and target rental return by 11:15-11:30. That supports flights after about 1:15, with 2:00-3:30 feeling more comfortable.
Okay. Hold the Sunday Delta and the Bloomington room. What return window should I pair with it?

Pair it with a Wednesday return no earlier than 1:15 p.m.; I’d prefer something in the 2:00-3:30 range so the Plymouth conversations do not make the morning feel brittle. If there is a nonstop in that window at a reasonable fare, hold it. If the only nonstop is much later, compare that against a one-stop option only if the layover is short and the total arrival home time is still reasonable.
Anything left before I book?

Book or hold in this order: Sunday afternoon SLC-MSP nonstop, Wednesday return after 1:15, MSP rental car Sunday evening to Wednesday late morning, then the Bloomington cancellable room. Before confirming the hotel, verify breakfast start time, parking included, cancellation deadline, and whether the rate is refundable. Let the St. Paul code sit only as a backup until its deadline. Also confirm Plymouth parking, reception parking in St. Paul, and where your shipped boxes will be held. Keep airfare, hotel, rental, gas, parking, tolls, and meal receipts together for reimbursement.
